chunks: Because allegiance is once and for all; it is not open to reconsideration nor is there any scope for fresh proceedings of election. He who remains out of it is deemed to be critical of Islam while he who prevaricates upon it is a hypocrite.

key_terms.الْخِيَارُ: Choice, option, or the right to decide
key_terms.بَيْعَةٌ: Allegiance or pledge of loyalty, specifically in a political or religious context
key_terms.طَاعِنٌ: Critic, detractor, or one who points out flaws
key_terms.مُدَاهِنٌ: One who compromises, prevaricates, or is insincere in allegiance

ai.seo_question: What is the nature of political allegiance (bay'ah) according to Imam Ali's letter to Muawiya?
ai.summary: Imam Ali defines political allegiance (bay'ah) as a singular, binding commitment that precludes repeated deliberation or renewed choice, establishing a clear dichotomy between those who withdraw and those who remain insincerely. This passage highlights the political theology of the early Caliphate, where consistency in loyalty is valued over pragmatic compromise, reflecting the Shia emphasis on steadfastness in leadership. The distinction between the 'critic' (kharij) and the 'compromiser' (mudahin) serves as a critical framework for evaluating political legitimacy and sincerity in governance.
